diagnostic_evidence.quote: By applying the trace theorem and a scaling of boundary norms, we can write

issues.failure_explanation: Two essential estimates in the proof are asserted, not established. (1) The inequality |vtilde - Pi^grad_k vtilde|_{1,K} <= C |vtilde - Pi^grad_k vtilde|_{1/2,dK} is credited to 'the trace theorem and a scaling of boundary norms', but the trace theorem gives the reverse direction. The stated inequality is a lifting estimate, false for general H^1 functions (any nonzero w in H^1_0(K) has zero trace but positive H^1 seminorm); vtilde - Pi^grad_k vtilde lies in the enlarged space with Laplacian in P_k, so it is not harmonic and harmonic lifting does not apply either. The estimate is nevertheless true, but only through a separate nontrivial argument: for a zero-trace function w of the enhanced space, the enhancement condition plus the projection property force L^2-orthogonality of w to all of P_k (which contains Delta w), hence w = 0, and a finite-dimensional norm equivalence with uniform constants is still required. (2) The concluding step needs ||vtilde + d_h - Pi^grad_k(vtilde + d_h)||_{0,K} <= C h ||vtilde + d_h||_{1,K} ('another scaling argument'), a Poincaré-type bound for the projection-kernel part that is nowhere proved (the kernel function does not have zero mean or zero trace in general). Without these, (eq:claim), and hence Proposition prop:added-3, is unproven as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the two asserted estimates by proved ones: an enhancement-based lifting estimate for functions in the enhanced space intersect ker(Pi^grad_k) (zero-trace kernel functions vanish by the L^2-orthogonality argument above, then finite-dimensional norm equivalence and scaling), and a Poincaré-type bound ||v_h - Pi^grad_k v_h||_{0,K} <= C h ||v_h||_{1,K} on V_k(K) via a compactness/scaling or dof-based argument.
issues.overall_effect: The stable-splitting estimate is unproven as stated. Although no later proof formally cites prop:added-3, the upper stability bound of a_h (prop:stab) is in fact equivalent to this splitting stability (see ISSUE-003), so the reliability of the method's stability analysis rests on this gap.
issues.title: Splitting-stability proof uses a misattributed lifting estimate and an unproven Poincaré-type kernel bound
issues.why_classification: The statement is true and no claim is lost, but repairing the proof requires contained nontrivial replacement arguments (a kernel argument plus norm equivalences), not a routine local edit.

issues.failure_explanation: The sole justification given for the unisolvency of the velocity dofs is the containment V_k(K) subset [W-tilde_{k+2}(K)]^2. This containment is false in general. Membership in the enhanced space of degree k+2 requires (v - Pi^grad_{k+2} v) orthogonal to monomials of degrees k+1 and k+2, a condition unrelated to and not implied by the degree-k enhancement defining W-tilde_k; in particular, the non-polynomial elements of B_{k+2\setminus k} (which exist, since dim B_{k+2\setminus k} = dim P_k - dim P_{k-2} exceeds the dimension of the polynomial bubbles) satisfy no such condition - only polynomial bubbles, for which Pi^grad_{k+2} p = p, meet it trivially. The containment for the W-tilde_k part fails for the same reason. The proposition itself is true (dofs #1-3 are unisolvent on the enhanced space, and dofs #4 together with the constraint of orthogonality to P_{k-2} determine the bubble via unisolvency of the moments on B_{k+2}), but the stated reasoning is unsound.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Delete the containment claim and prove unisolvency directly: dofs(v)#1-3 are the unisolvent dofs of the enhanced space for the vtilde component, and dofs(v)#4 together with the built-in orthogonality of the bubble to P_{k-2} give all moments against P_k, which are unisolvent on B_{k+2}.
issues.overall_effect: The justification of prop:added-4 is invalid; unisolvency of the velocity dofs, on which the well-definedness of the discrete problem and of the dofi-dofi stabilizations relies, must be established by a different (direct) argument.
issues.title: Unisolvency justified by a false containment in the enhanced degree-(k+2) space
issues.why_classification: A short routine direct argument repairs the proof with no loss; the proposition's statement and all downstream uses are unaffected.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: where we took into account that $a^\elementvem(\vtilde,\bollatest_h)=a^\elementvem(\Qnabla{k}\vtilde,\bollatest_h)$ thanks to~\eqref{eq:cross-zero0}--\eqref{eq:cross-zero}.

issues.failure_explanation: The proof of the upper bound ends with a_h(v_h,v_h) <= C* a(v_h,v_h) - a(Q^grad_k vtilde, d_h) <= C* a(v_h,v_h). The final step is valid only if a(Q^grad_k vtilde, d_h) >= 0, but this cross term - the H^1-semi-inner pairing of the enhanced-space kernel part with the bubble part - is indefinite and changes sign under vtilde -> -vtilde. In fact, because a_h drops the cross term (II) of the continuous form, the upper bound a_h .leq. a is equivalent to the stability of the splitting (Proposition prop:added-3): if the gradients of vtilde and d_h nearly cancel, a(v_h,v_h) is small while a_h(v_h,v_h) remains comparable to a(vtilde,vtilde) + a(d_h,d_h). The written proof never invokes prop:added-3, so the upper inequality of (eq:stab) is unproven as written.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Bound the dropped term by Cauchy-Schwarz and the splitting stability of Proposition prop:added-3: |a(Q^grad_k vtilde, d_h)| <= C ||v_h||^2_{1,K}, which combined with the previous estimates yields the upper bound.
issues.overall_effect: The upper bound of (eq:stab) is unproven; consequently the continuity claim of prop:cont-cor (which derives from prop:stab) and, transitively, the well-posedness and error results built on it lose their as-written support.
issues.title: Upper stability bound drops an indefinite cross term as if nonnegative
issues.why_classification: A short local repair using a proposition already in the paper restores the bound; no claim, constant type, or regime changes.

issues.failure_explanation: The stabilization bounds (eq:stab_ah) for S^K_{k+2} are assumed only for functions in the bubble space intersect ker(Pi^grad_{k+2}), i.e. for H^1_0 bubbles. The proof of prop:stab applies them to Q^grad_{k+2} d_h = d_h - Pi^grad_{k+2} d_h, which is in ker(Pi^grad_{k+2}) but not in H^1_0(K): the elliptic projection matches only the boundary mean, and Pi^grad_{k+2} d_h is in general nonzero on the boundary, so Q^grad_{k+2} d_h is not in the bubble space. Hence the upper bound step S_{k+2}(Q^grad_{k+2} d_h, Q^grad_{k+2} d_h) <= gamma* a(Q^grad_{k+2} d_h, Q^grad_{k+2} d_h) (active for beta_sharp > 0) and the refinement 'for beta_sharp >= 1/gamma_star, C = 1' invoke the assumption outside its hypotheses. Only the beta_sharp = 0 branch, used in all numerical tests, avoids these terms.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Either restrict the stability analysis to beta_sharp = 0 (dropping the beta_sharp > 0 option and the C = 1 refinement), or restate (eq:stab_ah) for S^K_{k+2} on the space where it is actually applied (the range of Q^grad_{k+2} on the bubble space) and verify that concrete stabilizations such as dofi-dofi satisfy it there.
issues.overall_effect: The stability of a_h for beta_sharp > 0 and the constant refinement 'C = 1 for beta_sharp >= 1/gamma_star' are unsupported; the beta_sharp = 0 configuration actually used in the paper and in all experiments remains covered by the valid parts of the proof.
issues.title: Bubble stabilization bounds applied outside their assumed domain
issues.why_classification: Repair requires either a limited weakening (restricting the theory to beta_sharp = 0) or restating the stabilization hypothesis on the correct space and verifying it, a contained but nontrivial task; the practically used configuration survives.

issues.failure_explanation: The VEM interpolant is defined only for H^1(K) cap C^0(K) functions, and its approximation estimates (Propositions prop:added-1 and prop:interp_enh) are proved only for data in H^{k+1}. The analysis nevertheless applies it to less regular data: in the proof of prop:added-6, v_I interpolates v(q_h) in [H^1_0(Omega)]^2, whose vertex and edge values are undefined and for which the used bounds ||v(q_h) - v_I||_0 <= C h ||v(q_h)||_1 and ||v_I||_1 <= C ||v(q_h)||_1 are not available; in the proof of thm:added-3, rho_I interpolates the dual pressure rho, which possesses only H^1 regularity; the statement of thm:est itself refers to u_I and p_I for a solution (u,p) in V x Q of unspecified regularity (p in L^2_0 need not even lie in H^1); and cor:added-1 derives its pressure rate from Proposition prop:interp_enh although p is only assumed in H^k while that proposition requires H^{k+1}. No H^1/H^k-data approximation result in the global (continuous) spaces is provided anywhere in the source.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For prop:added-6 and thm:added-3, replace the nodal interpolants of H^1 data by a well-defined, H^1-stable quasi-interpolant into the global spaces (or argue via smoothing/density), establishing the needed ||.||_0 <= C h ||.||_1 estimates and moment matching; for cor:added-1, invoke or prove the H^s-version pressure estimate ||p - p_I||_0 <= C h^k |p|_k instead of the H^{k+1}-only Proposition prop:interp_enh.
issues.overall_effect: The weak inf-sup proof (prop:added-6), the L^2 velocity proof (thm:added-3), the statement of thm:est (definition of u_I, p_I) and the convergence-rate claim of cor:added-1 all use interpolation outside its established scope; the well-posedness chain (prop:added-7, thm:added-2) inherits the gap through prop:added-6.
issues.title: VEM interpolant invoked outside its definition and outside the proven estimates for low-regularity data
issues.why_classification: All claims survive, but the repair needs a contained nontrivial construction (a quasi-interpolation lemma for H^1 data in the global VEM spaces) plus corrected estimate citations, which goes beyond a routine local edit.

issues.failure_explanation: The global pressure space is defined as Q_k = {q_h in Q = L^2_0(Omega) : q_h in Q_k(K) for all K}. Unlike the velocity space, which inherits conformity from V = [H^1_0]^2, this definition imposes no continuity across element interfaces, and the literal reading admits discontinuous piecewise enhanced functions. The proof of prop:added-6 then integrates b(v(q_h) - v_I, q_h) by parts elementwise and asserts that the boundary term vanishes 'because v(q_h) and v_I have zero trace on the boundary of Omega', addressing only the outer boundary. Cancellation on interior interfaces requires q_h to be single-valued there; this is an unstated hypothesis that the stated definition of Q_k does not provide, so the step is unjustified as written.

failure_location.quote: where the boundary term vanishes because $\v(q_h)$ and $\v_I$ have zero trace on $\partial\Omega$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the intended conformity condition to the definition of the global pressure space (q_h continuous across element interfaces, i.e. Q_k contained in the globally continuous enhanced space with zero mean), which makes the trace cancellation valid.
issues.overall_effect: Under the literal definition of Q_k, the key integration-by-parts step of the weak inf-sup proof fails, and the well-posedness and error results built on prop:added-6 presuppose an unstated conforming reading of the pressure space.
issues.title: Global pressure space defined without the conformity its analysis requires
issues.why_classification: A one-line local change to the definition (a standard local condition) repairs the defect with no loss of any claim or guarantee.

issues.failure_explanation: Proposition prop:added-7 - the discrete inf-sup and continuity of B_h, on which unique solvability (thm:added-2) and the entire error analysis rest - is 'proved' by a single sentence deferring to an adaptation of [Theorem 4.5, guo2020new]. The cited theorem is established for a different discretization with different bilinear forms and spaces; the source contains no argument and no verification that the hypotheses of that theorem (coercivity, weak inf-sup, and continuity of the specific forms) transfer to a_h, b_h, c_h on V_k x Q_k. The central well-posedness result is thus unsupported by the source alone.

failure_location.quote: The result is proved by adapting~\cite[Theorem 4.5]{guo2020new}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Supply the standard stabilized saddle-point inf-sup argument in the source: combine coercivity/continuity of a_h (prop:cont-cor), the weak inf-sup of prop:added-6, and continuity of b_h and c_h, verifying that the pattern of the cited theorem applies to these forms.
issues.overall_effect: The discrete inf-sup and continuity of B_h, hence the unique-solvability and stability statement of thm:added-2 and the error estimates that use the discrete well-posedness, rest on an argument not present in the source.
issues.title: Central discrete inf-sup proof entirely deferred to an adaptation of an external theorem
issues.why_classification: The result follows by a standard, contained argument from ingredients already in the paper; only the missing proof must be written out, with no change to any statement.

issues.failure_explanation: In deriving (eq:a_1) the proof splits a_h^K(u_I - Pi^grad_k u, v_h) - whose first argument does lie in V_k(K) - into a_h^K(u_I - u, v_h) + a_h^K(u - Pi^grad_k u, v_h). By its definition (eq:ah), a_h^K is defined only on V_k(K) x V_k(K), since it uses the (utilde, bubble) decomposition of its arguments; u_I - u and u - Pi^grad_k u involve the continuous solution u and are not in V_k(K), so both terms are undefined as written (the same expressions reappear in the subsequent assembly of B_h[(u_I-u_h,p_I-p_h),.]). Only their sum is meaningful, and the bounding must be carried out on the sum.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep the terms combined as a_h^K(u_I - Pi^grad_k u, v_h) (both arguments in V_k(K)) and bound it via the continuity of a_h (prop:cont-cor) plus the triangle inequality ||u_I - Pi^grad_k u||_1 <= ||u - u_I||_1 + ||u - Pi^grad_k u||_1, never splitting a_h across non-discrete arguments.
issues.overall_effect: The manipulation leading to (eq:a_1) and to the final bound of thm:est manipulates undefined quantities; the estimate is recoverable, and the corollary and L^2-velocity theorem that build on thm:est inherit the as-written gap.
issues.title: Main error proof evaluates a_h at arguments outside its domain of definition
issues.why_classification: A routine local rewriting (do not distribute a_h; use its continuity) yields exactly the stated bound, with no loss.

issues.failure_explanation: In (eq:VI) the proof expands c_h(p_h, rho_I) as -c_h(p - p_h, rho_I) + c_h(p, rho_I) and bounds it through the stabilization assumption (eq:stab_sp). That assumption is stated only for functions in Q_k(K) cap ker(Pi^0_k), and c_h is defined on Q_k; p - p_h and p (the continuous pressure) are not in Q_k, so Q^0_k(p - p_h) does not belong to Q_k(K) and the polarization bound |S_p^K(q_1,q_2)| <= delta* ||q_1||_0 ||q_2||_0 is not available for these arguments. The estimate of this term in the duality proof is therefore unsupported as written. (The proof of thm:est treats the analogous term via the interpolant p_I in Q_k, which is the routine repair.)
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace p by the interpolant p_I in Q_k in the c_h terms (as thm:est already does), so that both arguments lie in Q_k cap ker(Pi^0_k) where (eq:stab_sp) applies; the final bound is unchanged since ||Q^0_k(p_h - p_I)||_0 and ||Q^0_k p_I||_0 are controlled by ||p - p_h||_0, ||p - p_I||_0 and ||p - Pi^0_k p||_0.
issues.overall_effect: The bound (eq:VI), and hence the L^2 velocity estimate of thm:added-3, is incomplete as written, though its conclusion is expected to hold.
issues.title: L^2-velocity proof invokes c_h and its stability bound outside the assumed class
issues.why_classification: A routine local substitution (already used elsewhere in the paper) restores the argument with the same final estimate.

issues.failure_explanation: The reported mesh data cannot describe the meshes used. In the Voronoi column, h = 0.0375 at Level 1 (64 elements) and h = 0.189 at Level 2 (256 elements): the mesh size increases under refinement while the hexagon column on the same rows decreases (0.290 to 0.144), and 64 elements of diameter 0.0375 cannot cover the unit square; Levels 3-4 give 0.049 and 0.038, again below the Level-2 value, so the Voronoi h-column is erroneous. Moreover, the random-polygon rows violate the planar Euler relation N_V - N_e + N_K = 1 satisfied exactly by the hexagon, Voronoi and diamond columns (e.g. 256 - 331 + 64 = -11; 501 - 656 + 128 = -27; 13350 - 17985 + 4096 = -539), so these counts cannot describe conforming polygonal meshes of a simply connected domain under the counting convention of the other columns.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the erroneous entries: the Voronoi h-values must decrease monotonically under refinement and be consistent with the element counts, and the random-polygon vertex/edge/element counts must satisfy the planar Euler relation (or the differing counting convention must be stated and corrected).
issues.overall_effect: The table that labels the convergence study (mesh sizes and counts underlying the reported convergence plots and the numerical confirmation of the theory) contains mutually inconsistent, mathematically impossible values.
issues.title: Mesh data table is internally inconsistent
issues.why_classification: A data correction that affects no theoretical claim; the inconsistency is decisive but local to the numerical metadata.

issues.failure_explanation: The prose claims that all numerical tests confirm the theoretical estimates. However, the manufactured pressure of Test 2 has nonzero mean: the first term (4x^3-6x^2+2x)(2y^3-y) integrates to zero over the unit square, the second term (1/5)(6x^5-15x^4+10x^3)y has mean (1/5)(1/2)(1/2) = 1/20, and the constant contributes -1/10, so the total mean is 1/20 - 1/10 = -1/20. Hence p does not belong to Q = L^2_0(Omega), while the discrete pressure p_h in Q_k subset L^2_0(Omega) necessarily has zero mean. Consequently the reported error ||p - Pi^0_k p_h||_{0,Omega} is bounded below by |mean of p| = 1/20 and cannot converge to zero, contradicting the confirmation claim for Test 2's pressure as stated. (The constant should be -1/20, or the mean should be subtracted in the error computation.)

failure_location.quote: From the convergence plots, it is evident that the estimates presented in Section~\ref{sec:error_analysis} are confirmed by all the numerical tests and satisfied for all values of polynomial accuracy.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct the constant in Test 2's pressure so that the mean vanishes (replace -1/10 by -1/20), or subtract the mean of p when computing the pressure error; then the confirmation claim is consistent with the data.
issues.overall_effect: The claim that the numerical tests confirm the error estimates is not supported by the stated Test 2 data, whose pressure is incompatible with the zero-mean requirement of both the continuous and discrete problems; the Test 2 pressure convergence results are unreliable as reported.
issues.title: Test 2 manufactured pressure has nonzero mean, incompatible with the zero-mean pressure space
issues.why_classification: The repair is a single forced correction of a constant (uniquely determined by the zero-mean requirement) that restores the consistency of the test; no theoretical claim is affected.
